files.README.md:
# SQLite and local status

Create a Service connection with serviceType `sqlite`. Nonsecret settings:

```json
{"path":"/data/app.sqlite","queries":[{"name":"recent","label":"Recent jobs","sql":"SELECT id, status, created_at FROM jobs ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 100"}]}
```

The path is resolved inside the Homarr process/container. Mount the application's database (and SQLite WAL/SHM companions when applicable) read-only and ensure the Homarr user can read them. Prefer an application-supported backup/snapshot for a busy database. This adapter uses Node 24's built-in node:sqlite; no npm or HTTP connection is needed. Each invocation opens read-only and closes its own connection. Only owner-configured named queries are accepted from viewers, and results are bounded. Add an indexed LIMIT to expensive queries; the worker deadline cancels excessively slow handlers.

Optionally bind a serviceType `file` connection to status with settings {"path":"/data/status.json"}. It reads bounded JSON, checks the file size, and closes the descriptor. The files and SQL remain local connection settings and are not exported with the widget.

Diagnose checks file readability. Run preview to verify SQLite format, SQL and JSON parsing. Source: https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v24.x/api/sqlite.html
